_comment: Asha declarative PreToolUse policy rules. Evaluated by hooks/handlers/policy-guard.sh. User overrides/additions: ~/.asha/policies.json (merged by id, user wins). Schema per rule: {id, tool (anchored ERE on tool_name), command_regex|file_path_regex, action: deny|ask|warn (warn is awareness-only), exclude_regex?, reason, override_env?}. This is a soft string-pattern deterrent, not containment; pair it with the harness's permission and sandbox controls.

rules._comment: v3 after the 2026-08-04 adversarial review: targets now include ~, $HOME, quoted and doubled-slash forms (the most natural accidental phrasings all bypassed v2 — grep -r pattern ~ was ALLOWED); grep arm tolerates flags before the recursive flag (--include=*.md -R); [^|;&] stops the tool arm crossing && into an unrelated path (v2 denied 'find ./src -name x && cd /home/alice'). Scoped forms (~/Code, $HOME/Code, /home/user/dir) stay allowed. Round 2 added ~user (find ~alice scans another account's whole home and was allowed). Known residuals: an expanded-at-runtime variable other than $HOME still passes (the guard sees the unexpanded string), and 'grep -- -r ~' / 'grep -e -r ~' deny despite -r being a pattern argument there — rare enough to accept as safe-side noise.
rules.reason: Blocked broad scan over /home — unscoped find/grep/bfs/fd/rg across a whole home directory can cause severe disk pressure. Scope to a subdirectory, or set ASHA_ALLOW_BROAD_SCAN=1 to allow. Tune or remove this rule in ~/.asha/policies.json if it does not fit your machine.

rules._comment: 2026-08-07 cross-repo arm (workspace v1, delivery issue 5 of docs/proposals/2026-08-06--workspace-memory.md): optional global flags -C <path> / --git-dir[=]<path> / --work-tree[=]<path> — quoted, attached (-C/ws), =, repeated, and MIXED-quoted ("$ROOT"/shared) forms — are consumed between `git` and the verb; `git -C /ws push --force` previously evaded every arm because the verb had to directly follow `git`. Pass-2 hardening (PR #30 codex review): the arg matcher accepts composed quoted/unquoted runs, exclusions are segment-scoped (git[[:space:]][^|;&]* prefix — `... push --force && echo --force-with-lease` no longer launders the deny; same fix class as destructive-delete v2.4.0), and the evaluator normalizes backslash-newline continuations before matching (policy-guard.sh). Env-prefixed forms (GIT_DIR=/x git push --force) were already caught: the pattern is unanchored, so the inner `git push` substring matches. Known residuals, accepted: other global flags (-c <k>=<v>, --no-pager, --exec-path, -P) can still precede the verb and evade — widening to a generic pre-verb flag matcher is a separate Keeper decision (over-broad guards get disabled; see destructive-delete history); an unquoted backslash-escaped-space path (-C /work\ space) evades toward ALLOW; and quoted TEXT that merely mentions a guarded command (a commit message quoting a cross-repo force-push) false-positives toward DENY — safe-side, reword the message. Cross-repo plain commit/push stays allowed by design (workspace saves; Test 104 xr_* pins).
rules.reason: Blocked destructive git operation — irreversible, or affects shared state. Discarding uncommitted work (checkout --, restore, clean -f) has no reflog: use `git stash` instead, which is recoverable. Force-push: use --force-with-lease, which is permitted. History rewrites (filter-repo, filter-branch) invalidate every existing clone and cannot be undone once pushed — re-verify the blast radius, and prefer a fresh repo over rewriting a shared one. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_GIT=1 to allow.

Blocked rm of an archive or shell glob. Deleting an archive before its contents are extracted AND verified is the incident class this rule exists for — extract first, confirm the files are readable, then remove, or move to `.trash/` instead. This arm deliberately has NO path exemptions (not even /tmp/): an archive is unextracted data wherever it sits, and a path exemption anywhere in the command previously suppressed protection for every other target on the same line. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DELETE=1 to allow.
rules._comment: Ordered before destructive-delete so on a double match THIS rule's incident-specific reason surfaces (an excluded rule continues to the next rule rather than allowing, so ordering picks the reason, not the outcome — round-2 review corrected an earlier overstatement here). Empty path-exemption budget is the mixed-target fix ('rm -rf /tmp/extract pdfs.7z' was ALLOWED because /tmp/ matched the general rule's exclude). Middle class is [^|;] — & deliberately allowed so a quoted 'backup&old.7z' is reachable; terminator ["']?([[:space:];|&]|$) covers quoted names and adjacent operators ('rm backup.7z&&ls' slipped v2). Known accepted false positive: 'rm -f a.txt && ls x.7z' denies (the middle crosses && to the archive) — safe-side, override hint shown. To relax archive deletion a user must override BOTH delete rules in ~/.asha/policies.json: they overlap on flag-carrying archive deletes, and overriding only this one leaves destructive-delete denying. Overrides replace in place (position = priority).

rules.reason: Blocked irreversible deletion (rm -r/-f, shred, gh repo delete). Prefer moving to a `.trash/` staging dir over deleting outright. Regenerable trees (node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, /tmp), package/container removal (git rm, npm rm, docker rm), and Asha's own Work/markers/ files are exempt. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DELETE=1 to allow.
rules._comment: Reworked after the 2026-08-04 adversarial review. Path exemptions are now scoped to the rm segment itself (rm[[:space:]]["']?[^|;&]*(...)) — previously '/tmp/' ANYWHERE in the command suppressed the rule, so 'rm -rf important && mkdir -p /tmp/stage' was ALLOWED. Work/markers/ exemption fixes the review's BLOCKER: /rp:end, /rp:start, /session:silence and /session:restore all instruct 'rm -f Work/markers/<x>' and were denied by v1 — a guard that blocks its own toolkit's shipped cleanup gets overridden into uselessness. Known residual, accepted: a manager-prefix in a LATER segment ('rm -rf x; git rm y') still suppresses, because ERE cannot tie that exclusion to the segment that matched; and mixed targets inside ONE rm where an exempt path sits beside a precious NON-ARCHIVE target ('rm -rf /tmp/a precious-dir') are still suppressed — the archive rule above removes the worst class. This is a string-pattern deterrent, not containment (see file _comment).

rules.reason: Blocked direct edit to published Memory. Use the explicit save publisher or set ASHA_ALLOW_MEMORY_EDIT=1 for reviewed migration.

File written into a content root (Vault/Lore/Wiki/Codex/Compendium/Archive) outside its expected top-level buckets (World/Books/Sessions/Characters/Templates/Resources). Warn-only: this is a scatter check, not a block.
rules._comment: The content root must stay a named anchor, not a wildcard. The root list is portable and extensible; the taxonomy is project-specific. Warn-only by design: a wrong root list never blocks a write.

Structural approval split (Keeper ruling 2026-08-22): approval verbs are operator acts from the Keeper's own terminal. The controller refuses every operator write from the coordinator's pane and from any session whose environment carries ASHA_ORCHESTRATION_COORDINATOR_ID; that is the braces. This rule is a belt that applies only when the variable is present in the harness process environment at launch (hooks do not see a shell export made inside the session).
rules.reason: Operator approval verbs are refused inside a coordinator session. Approve, reject, or approve salvage from your own terminal (asha control or the CLI outside the coordinator pane).
